summary: Ivo Fišer (1929–2004) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer at Charles University in 1959 and held a post in the Institute for Indian Philology at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1971 to 1999.

Iwao Nakajima (born 1934) is a religious studies scholar. He completed a master's degree at Hitotsubashi University, studying under Nichiki Kimura, and later held positions at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute (until 1975) and at Sandhaan as 主幹.

Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya University from circa 1969 to 1978 and later served as a professor at Kanazawa University from circa 1996 to 2007.

Izumi Hoshi (born 1967) is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1986 to 1996 and served as an associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2003.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology who studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. She held a post at the University of Washington, where she taught Qian Lin.

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1953–1956) and the University of Chicago (~1961–1979), teaching Yasuke Ikari and W. Randolph Kloetzli.
J. B. Disanayaka (born 1937) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at SOAS University of London and at the University of Colombo, where he was a professor from circa 1982 to 2002.

J. C. Cleary (1947–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Harvard University (~1975–1985) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi and committee member Tu Weiming, and he served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

J. Estlin Carpenter (1844–1927) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of London from circa 1860 to 1866 and later held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1886 to 1915.

J. G. de Casparis (1916–2002) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held posts at SOAS University of London (~1957–1979), where he taught David N. Lorenzen, and as a professor at Leiden University (~1979–1986).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton (born 1942) studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He directed the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).

J. Talboys Wheeler (1824–1897) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford and served as Assistant Secretary to the Government of India from circa 1862 to 1870.

Jack Kornfield (born 1945) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1963–1967), held a post at Spirit Rock Meditation Center around 1987, and taught Jon Kabat-Zinn and Edward Espe Brown.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD from McMaster University between circa 1993 and 1999. He later held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1996–2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., and held posts at Yale (2005), SOAS (~2005–2008), and UC Berkeley (~2008 onwards) as Prof. Dr.
Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University (~2010–2013) under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.

Jacob N. Kinnard works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at William & Mary from circa 1998 to 2005 and held a post at the Iliff School of Theology around 2005.

Religious studies scholar Jacob Neusner (1932–2016) studied at Harvard, Lincoln College, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. His career included posts at Brandeis, UW-Milwaukee, the University of South Florida (~1990–2000), and Bard College (~1994–2014) as a Distinguished Service Professor.

Jacob Samuel Speyer (1849–1913) was an Indologist who studied under Hendrik Kern (~1867–1872). He held academic posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), the University of Groningen (1889–1903), and as Professor of Indology at Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel (1853–1938) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey (~1873–1874). He held professorial posts at the University of Basel (1881–1902) and the University of Göttingen (~1902–1915).
